resources.string: Keep Komora open until the download finishes.
Updating Komora. It will close and can be opened again.
Android asks for this once. Tap Allow, turn on \"Allow from this source\", then go back. Komora installs only the apps in this list.
Every file is checked before installing: it must be signed with the key Komora knows for that app. A file signed by anyone else is refused.

© Komora authors. Free software under the GNU GPL, version 3 or (at your option) any later version, without any warranty. Uses AndroidX and Kotlin libraries (Apache 2.0). Apps are downloaded from GitHub, which sees the address of the phone that asks.
No connection to GitHub. Check the internet and try again.
GitHub asks to wait (too many checks). Try again in an hour.
The latest release has no suitable app file.
The download stopped. Check the internet and tap the button again.
Not enough free space on the phone.
The file could not be read as an app. Nothing was installed.
The file holds a different app than expected. Nothing was installed.
The file is not signed with the expected key. Nothing was installed.
You already have this version or a newer one.
This app is already on your phone from another source, so Komora cannot update it. To switch: save its data, remove it (this deletes its data), then install it here.
Android did not install the app. Try again; if it repeats, restart the phone.
It needs the internet (GitHub only) and permission to install apps; notifications only if you turn on update notices. No accounts, no ads, no tracking.
Once a day Komora asks GitHub in the background and tells you when an app on this phone has a new version. Installing still happens here.
Android does not allow Komora\'s notifications. They can be allowed in the phone\'s settings.

Adds a second tab where you can add any public GitHub repository. Komora did not check those apps: you decide whom to trust. Their key is pinned at the first install, and every update must have the same key.
Komora has not checked these apps. Before the first install it shows the app\'s name, package and signing key; after you agree, only updates signed with the same key are installed.
Added by you. Komora has not checked this app: only that every update is signed with the same key as the first install.
From Komora\'s own list. The key is built into Komora; an APK with any other key is refused.
A link to a public GitHub repository that publishes APK files in its Releases.
The release has several APK files. Pick the one for this phone (usually \"universal\" or \"arm64\"). Komora will take the file with the same name in later releases.
That does not look like a GitHub repository. Example: github.com/owner/name
This app is already in Komora\'s own list.
You can add up to 20 sources.
This repository has no published release (or it does not exist).
The latest release has no APK files.
This app is already in Komora\'s list, or added from another source.

If you agree, Komora remembers this key. Every update must be signed with it, otherwise it is refused.
